prepare technique
An npm package lifecycle script stage that can run commands while a JavaScript package is being prepared or installed.
Previdian organization
Previdian is a named organization, product, or service referenced in security reporting.
Prism Medical Products organization
A medical-products organization referenced in security reporting.
Privacy laws concept
Rules that control how organizations may collect, use, share, and protect people’s personal information.
also: California’s tough privacy laws
Privacy Violations concept
Privacy violations are actions that improperly collect, use, expose, or share personal information.
Private information concept
Private information is personal or confidential data that should not be shared without permission.
private keys concept
Private keys are secret cryptographic values used to prove identity, decrypt data, or authorize cryptocurrency transactions.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileged access concept
Privileged access is a higher level of permission that lets a user or system make important changes or view sensitive information.
also: privileged roles
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
also: escalate privileges
Probe technique
A probe is an attempt to test a system for weaknesses or useful information before an attack.
Probes technique
Automated checks sent to systems to discover services, versions, or possible vulnerabilities.
process hardening technique
Security protections that make it harder for another program or user to inject code into a running process.
Profiling concept
Profiling is the practice of analyzing information about someone to infer their interests, behavior, or characteristics.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt injection technique
Prompt injection is a way of giving an AI system instructions that may make it behave in unintended ways.
also: prompt injection threats
prompting technique
Prompting is the practice of giving instructions and information to an AI model to guide its response.
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
Proof of Exploitation concept
Proof of exploitation is evidence that a vulnerability can actually be used to attack an affected system.
protected process concept
A Windows process given extra safeguards to prevent untrusted software from modifying or controlling it.
Protected Process Light concept
Protected Process Light is a Windows security feature that restricts other programs from tampering with protected processes, including some security products.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
proxy_pass technique
An nginx configuration directive that forwards web requests to another server.
public exploits concept
Public exploits are attack code or instructions available to anyone that show how to take advantage of a vulnerability.
Public GitHub Repositories concept
Public GitHub repositories are code projects that anyone on the internet can view and copy.
Public GitHub repository product
A public GitHub repository is a code project on GitHub that anyone on the internet can view.
Public internet concept
The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
public sector organization
Government organizations and publicly funded services.
Public web concept
The public web is the part of the internet that anyone can access without being on a private network.
Publish concept
Publish means making an application, webpage, or other content available for other people to access online.
purchase histories concept
Records showing what products or services a customer bought in the past.
PwC organization
PwC, short for PricewaterhouseCoopers, is a global professional services firm that also provides cybersecurity consulting and incident response services.
PwnKit vulnerability
The name for a Polkit vulnerability that can let a local Linux user gain administrator-level privileges.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
Python reverse shell technique
A Python-based method that makes an infected computer connect back to an attacker so the attacker can run commands remotely.
QiAnXin organization
QiAnXin is a Chinese cybersecurity company that provides security products and threat intelligence.
QR codes concept
QR codes are square barcodes that a phone camera can scan to open a link or read stored information.
quarantined concept
Quarantined means a suspicious file, email, or system has been isolated so it cannot easily cause harm while it is investigated.
Queens Public Library organization
A public library system serving the Queens borough of New York City.
also: The library
Rackspace organization
A company that provides cloud computing, hosting, and managed technology services.
Rackspace Spot product
A cloud platform for managing and running applications, including workloads on Kubernetes clusters.
Radware organization
A cybersecurity company that provides network and application security products and research.
ransom demand concept
A ransom demand is a message from criminals asking for payment, usually to unlock systems or stop leaked data from being published.
RansomHouse threat-actor
A cybercriminal group that specializes in data extortion, stealing sensitive files and threatening to leak them without necessarily encrypting them.
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
also: ransomware attacks, ransomware attack
Ransomware Actors threat-actor
Ransomware actors are criminals who use malware to lock or steal data and demand payment from victims.
Ransomware Evolution Report other
The Ransomware Evolution Report is a report that discusses ransomware activity, trends, or threat groups.
ransomware operators threat-actor
Ransomware operators are criminals who run attacks that lock or steal data and demand payment from victims.
Ransomware Recovery concept
A service that helps an organization restore systems or data after a ransomware attack.
RapidFort organization
RapidFort is a software security company focused on reducing and securing container and application components.
Rate limits technique
Rate limits are rules that restrict how many requests a person or program can make in a set time.
reachability concept
Reachability means whether one system, account, or network location can access another.
reachability analysis technique
Reachability analysis checks whether a vulnerable or risky piece of code can actually be reached and triggered in a real application.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
real-time data loss prevention technique
Security controls that immediately detect and block sensitive information from being sent or exposed in unsafe ways.
real-time visibility concept
Real-time visibility means being able to see what is happening in systems or networks as it happens, rather than after the fact.
Reasoning concept
Reasoning is the process of working through information logically to reach an answer or decision.
Reboot concept
A reboot means restarting a computer, phone, server, or other device.
Recall concept
Recall is a measurement of how many real problems a system successfully finds, such as how many actual vulnerabilities a scanner detects.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
also: Microsoft Graph reconnaissance
Reconnaissance commands technique
Reconnaissance commands are commands attackers use to learn about a computer, network, users, files, or security settings.
Recover concept
Recover is a cybersecurity function focused on restoring systems, data, and services after an incident.
Red team concept
The offensive security team that simulates real-world attacks to test an organization's defenses and improve security.
red teaming technique
Red teaming is an authorized exercise where security experts act like attackers to test an organization's defenses.
also: red team test, human red team
Redamon other
A named entity referenced in security reporting about ARTEX.
Redis product
Redis is a fast in-memory database often used for caching, queues, and real-time application data.
also: a Redis instance
refresh tokens concept
Refresh tokens are long-lived login tokens that let an app get new access tokens without asking the user to sign in again.
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
regression concept
A regression is a new defect that makes something stop working after a change or update.
regulator concept
A regulator is an organization that oversees and enforces rules in a specific area.
regulators organization
Regulators are government or official bodies that create and enforce rules for industries and organizations.
Rejetto HTTP File Server product
A software product for sharing and serving files over HTTP, also known as HFS.
Related domains concept
Related domains are internet domain names connected to the same organization, campaign, attacker, or investigation.
Related infrastructure concept
Related infrastructure means connected servers, domains, IP addresses, or services that are part of the same operation or environment.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
Release notes concept
Release notes are written summaries that explain what changed in a new software version.
remediate concept
To remediate means to fix a security problem or reduce the risk it creates.
remediated concept
Remediated means a security issue has been fixed or otherwise addressed.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
Remote access tools tool
Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote management and monitoring (RMM) tool
Software used by administrators to monitor, support, and control computers remotely.
remote management tools tool
Remote management tools let administrators control, monitor, or fix computers from another location, but attackers can also abuse them.
Remote Support product
Remote Support is software or a service that lets a technician connect to a user’s device from another location to help fix problems.
Remote Takeover technique
An attack in which someone gains control of a device or system from elsewhere over a network.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
also: RCE
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
repositories concept
Repositories are places where software project files and related development data are stored.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
Request-Time DNS technique
The practice of looking up a server name through DNS while handling a request instead of using a fixed address or group.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
resolver protocol
A resolver is a DNS component that looks up domain names and returns the matching internet addresses or records.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
response times concept
The duration between when a security incident occurs and when defenders begin containment or remediation; faster reduces damage.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
reusable connection concept
A reusable connection is a network connection marked as safe to keep open and use again for later requests.
also: reusable mark, reusable queue
Reverse proxies tool
Reverse proxies are servers that sit in front of web applications and forward requests to them, often adding security, caching, or load balancing.
reverse proxy tool
A reverse proxy is a server that sits in front of other servers and forwards user requests to them, often adding security or load balancing.
also: HTTP/2 reverse proxies, NGINX HTTP/2 reverse proxies
reverse shell technique
A reverse shell is a technique where a compromised computer connects back to an attacker and gives them a command-line session.
also: Python reverse shell payload, a reverse shell
ReversingLabs organization
ReversingLabs is a cybersecurity company that analyzes files, malware, and software supply-chain risks.
revocation concept
The process of invalidating a digital credential or certificate so it can no longer be used.
also: rapid revocation, withdraw its access
risk assessment concept
Risk assessment is the process of judging how likely and serious a security problem may be.
risk assessments concept
Risk assessments are reviews that identify what could go wrong and how serious the impact might be.
RMM tool
Software tools used by IT teams to manage computers remotely, sometimes abused by attackers to maintain persistent control over infected machines.
RMM tools tool
RMM tools are remote monitoring and management programs that let administrators manage computers from elsewhere.
root cause analysis concept
An investigation to identify the underlying reason a problem or security incident occurred.
root shell concept
A root shell is a command-line session with the highest administrator privileges on a Unix or Linux system.
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
root-level access concept
Root-level access is the highest level of control on many systems, allowing someone to change almost anything.
rotate secrets and credentials technique
To replace passwords, keys, tokens, and similar access information with new values after possible exposure.
Ruby tool
Ruby is a programming language used to build software and web applications.
rubygems
RubyGems is the package manager and public package repository for the Ruby programming language.
also: Ruby gems
run code on the server technique
To make a remote server execute commands or programs, potentially giving an attacker control over it.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
Runtime Bill of Materials concept
A Runtime Bill of Materials lists the software components that are actually present or loaded while an application is running.
Runtime Profiling technique
Examining a program while it runs to learn which code, components, or resources it actually uses.
runtime protection technique
Runtime protection watches software while it is running and blocks dangerous behavior as it happens.
Runtime security concept
Runtime security means protecting and monitoring software while it is actually running, not just before it starts.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russia-linked threat-actor
A description for threat actors or activity reported as having connections to Russia.
SaaS concept
SaaS is software delivered over the internet as a subscription or hosted service instead of installed and managed entirely by the customer.
SaaS applications concept
SaaS applications are software services delivered over the internet rather than installed and managed locally by each organization.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.
Sakura Internet organization
Sakura Internet is a Japanese internet and cloud services company.
SAML protocol
SAML is a standard that lets users sign in once and access multiple services by passing trusted identity messages between them.
also: SAML tokens, SAML signing key, token-signing key, STS signing certificate
SAML Signing Keys concept
Cryptographic keys used to sign SAML login tokens so systems can verify that they are legitimate.
sandbox concept
A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
sandboxed concept
Sandboxed means running software in a restricted environment so it has limited access to the rest of the system.
SARA product
A commercial security solution referenced in reporting.
also: NetSPI+Synack’s SARA
SAWSNAKE tool
A security tool referenced in reporting that is associated with carrying out Golden SAML attacks.
scammers threat-actor
Scammers are people who trick others to steal money, information, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
scgi_pass concept
An NGINX configuration directive that sends requests to an application server using the SCGI protocol.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
Scoring concept
Scoring is the practice of assigning a number or rating to show how risky, important, or suspicious something is.
Screen Share Guard product
A security feature that checks screen-sharing content and warns users when sensitive information may be visible.
Screen Sharing technique
A feature that lets someone else view the contents of your computer screen remotely.
screen-share concept
The act of allowing another person or application to view what is displayed on a device’s screen.
screenshots concept
Images that capture what is currently shown on a computer screen.
Secure Access concept
The ability for authorized people to safely reach systems, applications, or data while blocking unauthorized users.
Secure Remote Password protocol
A password-authentication protocol designed to let two parties verify a password without sending the password itself over the network.
also: SRP
Security advisories concept
Security advisories are notices that explain vulnerabilities, risks, and recommended fixes.
security checks technique
Security checks are tests or reviews used to find risks, weaknesses, or unsafe behavior in a system.
security controls concept
Security controls are safeguards, such as settings, tools, or policies, used to reduce risk.
Security incident concept
A security incident is an event where systems, data, or accounts may have been attacked, exposed, or misused.
Security incidents concept
Security incidents are events that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems or data.
security measures concept
Security measures are steps or tools used to reduce the chance or impact of security problems.
Security operations teams organization
Security operations teams monitor systems, investigate alerts, and respond to cyber threats inside an organization.
security policies concept
Security policies are rules that say how people and systems should protect data, accounts, and technology.
security posture concept
Security posture is the overall strength of an organization's defenses, risks, and readiness to handle cyber threats.
also: cybersecurity posture
security products concept
Software or hardware designed to protect systems from cyber threats, like antivirus or firewalls.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
security service edge concept
Security service edge is a cloud-delivered security model that protects web, cloud, and private-application access.
also: SSE
Security Settings concept
A configuration area where users manage an online service's security controls.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.
security testing concept
Security testing is checking software, systems, or networks to find weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.
Segmented technique
Segmented means a network or system has been divided into separate parts to limit access and reduce the spread of an incident.
self-defending infrastructure concept
Computing systems designed to automatically detect threats and protect themselves while continuing to operate.
self-hosted concept
Self-hosted means an organization runs software on servers it controls instead of using a vendor's cloud service.
self-hosted model concept
An AI model that an organization runs on its own systems or chosen cloud environment rather than using a public hosted service.
Self-Hosted Models concept
Self-hosted models are AI models that an organization runs on its own infrastructure instead of relying entirely on a cloud provider’s hosted API.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
Sensitive records concept
Sensitive records are stored pieces of information that could harm people or organizations if exposed.
separate infrastructure concept
Separate infrastructure means using distinct servers, networks, or accounts so one system is isolated from another.
server concept
A server is a computer system that provides services or resources to other computers or users.
also: N-able-hosted server, company-hosted server
server configuration concept
Settings and files that control how a server operates and connects to other systems.
server-side-request-forgery vulnerability
Server-side request forgery is a vulnerability that lets an attacker make a server send requests to places the attacker should not be able to reach directly.
also: SSRF
service account concept
A non-human account used by an application or service to perform automated tasks, often holding elevated privileges.
also: old service account
Service disruption concept
A service disruption is a period when an online service is unavailable, slow, or not working correctly for users.
service providers organization
Service providers are companies or organizations that deliver services such as internet access, hosting, software platforms, or managed IT support.
Setup concept
The process of preparing a device, application, or account for use.
severity concept
Severity is a rating that describes how serious a security issue is.
SFTP protocol
SFTP is a secure file transfer protocol that uses encryption to move files between computers.
SFTP Credentials concept
Usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used to access a server through Secure File Transfer Protocol.
shadow-ai
Shadow AI is the use of AI tools in an organization without official approval, visibility, or security oversight.
shell commands concept
Shell commands are text instructions typed into a command line to tell a computer what to do.
shinyhunters
ShinyHunters is a cybercrime group known for stealing and selling large databases of user information.
ShinyHunters threat-actor
ShinyHunters is a cybercriminal group known for data theft, extortion, and selling stolen information.
Shirudo tool
An open-source Linux security runtime that deploys temporary protections for vulnerable software without stopping the service.
also: Shirudo’s, The Shirudo project
shopping cart concept
A website feature that holds items a customer intends to purchase before checkout.
Short-Lived Credentials concept
Passwords, tokens, or keys that expire quickly so stolen access is useful for only a limited time.
shut down concept
Shutting down means fully turning off a computer rather than leaving it running or asleep.
SIEM product
A security tool that gathers and analyzes logs from across an organization in real time to spot suspicious activity.
Sign-In concept
Sign-in is the process of proving your identity to access a computer, account, or online service.
Signal product
A privacy-focused messaging app that encrypts calls and messages end-to-end, meaning only the sender and receiver can read them.
signature-based technique
Signature-based detection looks for known patterns that match previously identified malware or attacks.
Signers concept
Signers are people or systems that approve a transaction by applying a cryptographic signature.
signing technique
A cryptographic process that uses a private key to prove that data came from its owner and was not changed.
Signing certificate concept
A signing certificate is a digital credential used to prove that software, a document, or another certificate was approved by its stated signer.
signing key concept
A signing key is a cryptographic key used to prove that data, software, or a message really came from a trusted source and was not changed.
Signing keys concept
Signing keys are cryptographic keys used to prove that software or data really came from a trusted publisher and was not changed.
Single Sign On concept
Single Sign On lets a person log in once and then access multiple approved apps without signing in again each time.
also: vsphere.local
sitecustomize.py tool
sitecustomize.py is a special Python startup file that can run automatically whenever the Python interpreter starts.
situational awareness concept
An understanding of what is happening around an organization, including current threats and risks.
Skagerak Energi organization
A Norwegian electricity company.
slack
Slack is a workplace messaging and collaboration platform.
also: Slack API, Slack command channel
SmartConsole Authentication Bypass vulnerability
A security weakness that lets an attacker bypass sign-in checks in Check Point SmartConsole.
Smartphone product
A smartphone is a mobile phone that can run apps, access the internet, and store personal data.
Soapbox Engage product
An online fundraising and donation platform for nonprofit organizations.
SOAR product
SOAR, or security orchestration, automation, and response, is software that helps security teams automate investigations and response tasks.
SOC organization
SOC stands for security operations center, a team or function that monitors and responds to security issues.
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
also: social engineering attacks
socket organization
Socket is a software supply-chain security company that scans open-source packages for risky behavior.
also: Socket's
socket-certified-patches tool
A Socket tool or package used to obtain and apply vendor-provided patches for vulnerable software.
also: Socket patches, security patches
SOCs organization
SOCs, or Security Operations Centers, are teams and facilities that monitor, investigate, and respond to cybersecurity threats.
SoftEther VPN product
SoftEther VPN is an open-source VPN product used to create encrypted network connections between devices or networks.
software attack surface concept
A software attack surface is all the places in an application or system where an attacker might try to get in or cause harm.
Software Bill of Materials concept
A Software Bill of Materials is a list of the software components, libraries, and dependencies included in an application or device.
Software Bills of Materials concept
Software Bills of Materials are lists of the software components, libraries, and dependencies used inside an application.
Software Bug concept
A software bug is an error in a program that causes it to behave incorrectly or unexpectedly.
software development concept
Software development is the process of designing, writing, testing, and maintaining computer programs.
Software flaws vulnerability
Software flaws are mistakes or weaknesses in programs that can cause bugs or create security risks.
software supply chain risk concept
The risk that software is compromised through its developers, build systems, dependencies, or distribution process.
SolarWinds organization
SolarWinds is an IT management software company widely known for a major 2020 supply-chain breach affecting its Orion product.
also: software company SolarWinds
source code concept
The human-readable code written by programmers that makes up software.
source IP concept
A source IP is the internet address a network request appears to come from.
source IP addresses concept
Source IP addresses identify where network traffic appears to come from.
source-code access concept
Permission to view or change the human-readable programming instructions used to build software.
also: code access
south-korea
South Korea is an East Asian country often referenced in cybersecurity stories involving technology, espionage, or regional threats.
Spam concept
Spam is unwanted bulk messages, usually sent by email, text, or online platforms.
Spam filtering concept
Spam filtering is the process of identifying and blocking unwanted or suspicious email messages.
SpamExperts product
SpamExperts is an email-security service that filters spam and other unwanted or malicious messages.
also: SpamExperts Hosted Cloud Security Incident
SpamExperts Hosted Cloud product
A cloud-hosted email security service provided by N-able under the SpamExperts brand.
spearphishing technique
Spearphishing is a targeted scam message sent to a specific person or group to trick them into giving access or information.
spearphishing-link
A spearphishing link is a targeted phishing message that includes a malicious link tailored to a specific person or organization.
also: Spearphishing link (T1566.002)
SPF protocol
SPF is an email check that verifies whether a sending server is allowed to send email for a domain.
Spreadsheet concept
A grid-based file used to organize, calculate, and analyze data.
SQL injection technique
SQL injection is a web attack where malicious database commands are inserted into an application's input fields or requests.
SQL injection flaw vulnerability
A SQL injection flaw is a security weakness that can let an attacker send malicious database commands through an application's input fields.
SSH protocol
SSH is a secure way to remotely log in to and control another computer over a network.
also: SSH key, SSH sessions, SSH services, SSH logins
SSL VPN protocol
SSL VPN is a type of remote access connection that uses SSL-based security to connect users to a private network.
SSO concept
SSO, or single sign-on, lets a user sign in once and then access multiple connected apps without logging in separately to each one.
SSO Phishing technique
SSO phishing is a scam that uses a fake single-sign-on page to steal a person's work login details.
Stager technique
A small first-stage malware component that prepares a device to download or run additional malicious code.
Staging Environment concept
A staging environment is a test version of a system that closely resembles the live production system.
standing-privileges
Standing privileges are permanent access rights that remain available even when not needed, increasing risk if an account is compromised.
Startup concept
Startup usually refers to programs or scripts configured to run automatically when a computer or user session starts.
State Government Services concept
State government services are public services provided by a state government, such as licensing, benefits, or records access.
also: state services
state officials organization
State officials are government employees or leaders who work for a state government.
state-backed actors threat-actor
State-backed actors are hackers or groups that are supported, directed, or funded by a government.
state-backed groups threat-actor
State-backed groups are hacking or influence groups that are supported, directed, or protected by a national government.
static secrets concept
Static secrets are passwords, keys, or tokens that stay the same for a long time, making them risky if stolen.
Static Source-Code Pipeline technique
An automated process that examines program source code without running the program.
also: source-code pipeline
status page concept
A status page is a public or internal webpage that shows whether a service is working normally or having outages.
steal information technique
Steal information means to take data without permission, often to sell it, leak it, or use it for further attacks.
stealer log concept
A stealer log is a file or record created by information-stealing malware that contains stolen data such as passwords, cookies, or browser details.
STIX/TAXII protocol
STIX/TAXII are standards for describing and sharing cyber threat intelligence between tools and organizations.
Stolen concept
Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.
stolen access concept
Stolen access is unauthorized access to accounts, systems, or networks that criminals obtain and may sell to others.
stolen data concept
Stolen data is information taken without permission, often later sold, leaked, or used for extortion.
Stolen Funds concept
Money or other assets taken from their owner without permission.
Stolen Identity concept
A compromised account or set of identity details that an attacker can use while appearing to be a legitimate user.
stolen records concept
Stolen records are files or database entries taken without permission, often containing personal, financial, or business information.
Storage Volumes concept
Logical units of disk space that store files and data for computers, servers, or cloud services.
Stored concept
Stored is a ZIP entry type in which file data is saved without compression.
Stored passwords concept
Stored passwords are saved login credentials kept in a browser, application, password manager, or system.
Stored XSS vulnerability
Stored XSS is a web attack where malicious script is saved on a site and later runs in other users' browsers.
Storm-0940 threat-actor
A threat-actor group tracked by Microsoft in security reporting.
Streaming Platforms concept
Streaming platforms are online services that deliver music, video, or other media over the internet.
Strict concept
A security setting that applies stronger restrictions to reduce the chance of unauthorized access.
Strict Precision concept
A scoring approach that gives credit only for findings that are supported and correct.
also: precision
Subscription Keys concept
Subscription keys are secret values used to identify and authorize a customer or application when calling an API.
supply chain attack technique
A supply chain attack is when attackers compromise a trusted tool, service, or distribution path to reach its users.
supply chain risk concept
Supply chain risk is the danger that software, services, or vendors you rely on could introduce security problems into your own systems.
suspicious activity concept
Suspicious activity is behavior that looks unusual or risky and may indicate fraud, hacking, or policy violations.
Suspicious files concept
Suspicious files are files that look unusual or potentially harmful and may need investigation.
Synack organization
Synack is a cybersecurity company known for managed security testing and crowdsourced penetration testing services.
SYSTEM hive concept
A Windows Registry file that stores system configuration information and can contain data useful for recovering protected credentials.
also: registry hives
System Reconnaissance technique
The act of gathering information about a computer system after gaining access to it.
System Security concept
A log category or label used to identify security-related system events.
Systems Offline concept
A protective response in which computer systems are disconnected or shut down to limit possible damage.
also: take its systems offline
T1036 technique
T1036 is the MITRE ATT&CK technique ID for masquerading, where attackers make files, services, or activity look legitimate.
t1566-002
T1566.002 is the MITRE ATT&CK technique for phishing that uses malicious links in messages.
tactics concept
In cybersecurity, tactics are the broad goals behind an attacker's actions, such as gaining access, stealing data, or staying hidden.
TCP protocol
TCP is a core internet protocol that reliably sends data between computers by establishing a connection.
TCP port 2012 protocol
A numbered TCP network entry point, 2012, that software can use to accept connections.
also: port 2012
TeamPCP organization
TeamPCP appears to be a group or handle name, but I cannot define it confidently.
also: TeamPCP threat group
Technical analysis concept
Technical analysis is a detailed examination of how a system, vulnerability, malware sample, or attack works.
Technology companies organization
